vBRIEFInfo.author: overdeck/0.0.0
vBRIEFInfo.description: Plan for PAN-2336: fix create-beads.test.ts CI flake by mocking bd at the child_process.execFile callback level so real bd is never invoked

plan.title: bug(ci-flake): create-beads.test.ts intermittently fails in CI with 'table not found: issues' (beads DB setup race)
plan.author: agent:claude-opus-4-8

narratives.Problem: src/lib/vbrief/__tests__/create-beads.test.ts intermittently reddens main in CI with `[beads] bd ping failed (Error 1146 (HY000): table not found: issues)` and `beads probe failed after recovery`, yet passes 38/38 locally. Root cause (verified against main@60ce7c0362): beads.ts line 22 does `const execFileAsync = promisify(execFile)` — a one-time module-scope capture. Every bd call flows through execFileAsync. The test tries to intercept bd via `vi.mock('util', () => ({ promisify: () => mockExecAsync }))`, but that only works if beads.ts is evaluated AFTER the mock registers. When beads.ts is already in the fork's module registry (loaded transitively by a setupFile or a prior test), execFileAsync already holds realPromisify(realExecFile); the util mock cannot retroactively rebind it, so the REAL bd binary runs. In CI the redirect points at an uninitialized shared Dolt DB, so real `bd ping` fails with 'table not found: issues'. Local runs load beads.ts fresh with mocks in place, so they pass — this is the module-load-order split that makes the flake CI-only. The issue's own suggested fixes (deterministically provision the `issues` schema; make `bd doctor --fix` recover the table) are misdirected: the correct fix is to guarantee the real bd binary is never invoked by this fully-mocked test.
narratives.Proposal: Switch the mock strategy from util.promisify interception to a callback-level child_process.execFile mock, confined to the test file. Remove the `vi.mock('util', ...)` block entirely. Replace `vi.mock('child_process', () => ({ exec: vi.fn(), execFile: vi.fn() }))` with a mock whose execFile invokes its callback by routing through mockExecAsync: `execFile(file, args, opts, cb)` -> `mockExecAsync(file, args).then(r => cb(null, r.stdout, r.stderr), err => cb(err, '', ''))`. Because promisify wraps the execFile FUNCTION (a live binding), routing execFile itself through the mock intercepts bd regardless of when beads.ts was loaded or which promisify it captured. No production code changes; only the two vi.mock blocks change. Verify with a 20x CI-mode loop over the file plus one full-suite CI-mode run.
narratives.NonGoals:
- Do not modify beads.ts or any production code to accommodate test mocking (FR-4).
- Do not add maxForks:1, singleFork:true, or any suite serialization to mask the flake (FR-3); CLAUDE.md forbids masking OOM/flake this way.
- Do not add vi.resetModules()/dynamic imports as the primary fix; the callback-level mock is sufficient (reserved only as H1 fallback).
- Do not initialize a real beads/Dolt DB or change real `bd doctor --fix` recovery behavior; the fix prevents real bd from being invoked at all.
- Do not touch scripts/flaky-quarantine.txt; it does not exist on this branch (PRD W2 deferred until PAN-2373 lands).
- Do not introduce real setTimeout in delay paths or new explicit `any` (NFR-1).
- Do not rewrite existing test assertions, describe blocks, or the runCreateBeads/testSleep helpers beyond what the mock-signature change strictly requires.

autoDecisions.summary: Kept the fix as a single atomic bead touching only the two vi.mock blocks.
autoDecisions.rationale: The mock-strategy swap is genuinely indivisible — removing the util mock without adding the callback-level child_process mock leaves the suite hanging (no callback fires), so intermediate states are not independently mergeable. This is the rare indivisible change, so one bead is correct rather than an artificial split.

items.title: Mock bd at the child_process.execFile callback level so real bd is never invoked

verify_commands: for i in $(seq 1 20); do CI=1 npx vitest run src/lib/vbrief/__tests__/create-beads.test.ts || exit 1; done
expected_outputs: 20 consecutive CI=1 runs each exit 0 with no 'table not found: issues' error and no test timeout
full CI=1 npm test run shows no create-beads failures

narrative.Action: In src/lib/vbrief/__tests__/create-beads.test.ts: (1) DELETE the entire `vi.mock('util', async (importOriginal) => { ... promisify: () => mockExecAsync ... })` block (currently lines ~18-24). (2) REPLACE the `vi.mock('child_process', () => ({ exec: vi.fn(), execFile: vi.fn() }))` block (currently lines ~13-16) with one whose execFile is a vi.fn that invokes the trailing callback by routing through mockExecAsync: read the callback as the last argument, file as callArgs[0], args as (Array.isArray(callArgs[1]) ? callArgs[1] : []), then `void mockExecAsync(file, args).then(r => cb(null, r.stdout, r.stderr), err => cb(err, '', ''))`. This works even when beads.ts captured execFileAsync before the mocks applied, because promisify(execFile) wraps the execFile function (a live binding) — routing execFile through the mock intercepts every bd call regardless of load order. (3) Keep the hoisted mockExecAsync and all existing per-test .mockResolvedValueOnce/.mockRejectedValueOnce/.mockImplementation sequences unchanged. (4) Re-verify every mockExecAsync.mock.calls.find/filter(([file, args]) => ...) site (which / bd init / bd create / bd delete / bd doctor --fix) still matches now that the mock is called as (file, args) with opts dropped; the --metadata/--deps JSON.parse sites read args[] only and are unaffected. Reproduce the flake first (H4: CI=1 loop) to confirm the mechanism, apply the change, then re-run to confirm green. Do NOT touch beads.ts or any production file.

items.title: The vi.mock('util', ...) block is removed and vi.mock('child_process', ...) invokes the execFile callback through mockExecAsync, so every bd invocation routes to the mock and no real bd subprocess is spawned even when beads.ts was loaded before the mocks applied.
`npx vitest run src/lib/vbrief/__tests__/create-beads.test.ts` exits 0 and reports 38 passed / 0 failed, with the existing per-test mock sequences and assertions unchanged.

20 consecutive `CI=1 npx vitest run …create-beads.test.ts` invocations each exit 0 and produce no `table not found: issues` error and no test-timeout, and one full `CI=1 npm test` run shows no create-beads failure.

Each mockExecAsync.mock.calls.find/filter(([file, args]) => …) assertion (which / bd init / bd create / bd delete / bd doctor) still resolves after the mock is called as mockExecAsync(file, args) with opts dropped.
